title: Signal Accord: Model & Route Metrics Grid (prototype & chart specs)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Overview: Create a compact, scan-friendly grid view that surfaces per-model and per-route performance and cost signals for the Redwood Console. Goal is a single-pane overview for engineers and PMs to triage regressions quickly and then deep-link into model/run-level traces. Scope: grid + row-level drill actions, small multiples of latency/throughput/token metrics, lightweight sparklines, cost delta badges, and a token-flow microtrace. Constraints: must reuse existing chart primitives where possible, be responsive down to 960px, and work with aggregated telemetry (1m/5m buckets). Acceptance criteria: 1) At-a-glance identification of routes with >10% p95 latency regression; 2) Inline cost-per-token delta shown alongside RPS; 3) Each row has quick actions: open route timeline, open model variant rollouts, start an eval; 4) Chart interactions respect SLO guardrails (hover shows p50/p95/p99 and sample count); 5) Design tokens and accessible color contrasts documented.
chart_spec_summary: Latency ribbon: compact stacked bands showing p50/p95/p99 per minute (min-height 28px). Tooltip shows sample N, anomalies flagged when p95 rises > 10% vs baseline.
Throughput sparkline + RPS band: line for avg RPS with shaded CI (stddev), secondary bar for concurrent requests. Toggle between absolute and normalized per-capacity.
Token flow microtrace: condensed waterfall showing input tokens, KV-hit savings, generated tokens; shows median token-path and % cache hit. Render as fixed-width micro bars to line up across rows.
Cost delta badge: small inline chip that computes recent cost per 1k tokens vs previous window; red/orange/green thresholds and hover shows calculation formula and sample size.
Request distribution histogram: small bar histogram for request size (tokens) binned, with median marker and ability to exclude outliers (top 1%).
Drill-on-click: opening a row expands to full trace canvas (route timeline) and deep-links to existing model route performance inspector.
comments: 2026-02-20 – Kickoff: scoped initial concept with PM (Lina Xu) and Eng lead (Ravi Shah). Agreed to prioritize per-route regressions and cost deltas in the grid. Action: produce low-fi wireframes for 2 use cases (regression triage, cost optimization).

2026-02-25 – Low-fi review: Wireframes posted to Drive (see attachments). PM asked to add 'compare to baseline' toggle; Eng flagged concerns about cost calc frequency for large tenants (sampling strategy required).

2026-03-01 – Prototype: High-fi Figma prototype created (frame: Signal Accord Grid) with interactive row expansion and hover tooltips. Added accessibility color tests. Shared with UX research for quick moderated sessions. Drive link and Figma link in attachments.

2026-03-03 – Usability study (n=6 engineers): participants located regressions faster with grid vs current list. Feedback: token-flow microtrace useful but needs clearer legend and lower visual noise. Action: simplify microtrace glyphs and add persistent legend toggle.

2026-03-05 – Eng review (ENG-19088): Engineering confirmed data availability for p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-request histograms. Raised two implementation trade-offs: 1) precomputed aggregates vs on-demand rollups for custom time windows; 2) storing cost-per-token for historical comparison may increase storage costs. Decided on 1m pre-aggregates + 5m rollups, and compute cost delta at query-time with cached baseline for heavy customers.

2026-03-08 – PM feedback (Lina Xu): Requested an export CSV action for selected rows and an API endpoint to fetch grid rows for automation. Also asked to include a 'last deploy' tag per route. Added to dependencies (ENG-19321 for API).

2026-03-09 – Design iteration: tightened chart spacing, introduced micro-legend, added keyboard focus states for row actions. Prepared spec sheet for front-end: exact token-width, font sizes, color hex values, and animation durations. Spec posted to Confluence and linked in attachments.

2026-03-10 – This ticket moved to In Review: design review scheduled with product and front-end on 2026-03-11. Remaining items: a) finalize sample-size notes for cost delta calculations; b) accessibility QA pass; c) update release notes draft. Follow-ups assigned as sub-issues.
